title: Software Engineer, Feature Engineering Platform
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Role

We’re building a new Feature Engineering Platform that will be the front door to ML development at global scale. As a Software Engineer on this team, you’ll help build a seamless experience for ML practitioners across the company - from experimentation and exploration to deployment and monitoring.

Our mission is to make machine learning accessible and intuitive without compromising on power or performance. You’ll work on a layered platform that supports both high-level declarative workflows and lower-level imperative APIs, all integrated into the environments our users already work in (like notebooks and internal sandboxes).

What You’ll Do

• Build and evolve APIs, SDKs, and platform integrations that power feature engineering workflows.

• Help shape user-facing tools to make the platform approachable for all skill levels.

Remote | Skin Clinic | 30 Hours/Week | $6.5/Hour

We are looking for a reliable and experienced Virtual Medical Assistant / Medical Receptionist to support a busy US-based skin clinic. This role will focus on frontline patient communication, scheduling, insurance verification, and administrative support so the in-clinic team can focus on direct patient care. The clinic serves a high volume of Spanish-speaking patients, so strong bilingual communication in Spanish and English is required.

We are looking for an individual who is naturally warm , friendly , and deeply empathetic .
You must bring a welcoming energy not only to the patients calling in but also to your relationship with the clinic staff.

Phone Management

• Answer inbound calls promptly and professionally.

• Assist patients with questions, appointment needs, and general clinic inquiries.

Appointment Scheduling

• Reschedule, cancel, and update appointments as needed.

• Confirm appointment details and help maintain an organized daily schedule.

Insurance Verification

• Verify patient insurance coverage and eligibility.

• Confirm active benefits, plan details, and patient responsibility when needed.

Prior Authorizations

• Must be fully fluent in both Spanish and English .

• Minimum of 1 year of experience supporting a US-based medical clinic .

• Strong experience with medical receptionist or front desk tasks.

• Comfortable handling patient calls in a busy healthcare setting.

• Knowledge of insurance verification and prior authorization workflows.

• Organized, dependable, detail-oriented, and able to work independently.

• Must be comfortable working remotely in a dedicated clinic support role.

Schedule and Work Setup

• 30 hours per week .

• Remote work setup.

• Immediate hiring need.

Ideal Candidate Profile
This role is best suited for someone who is polished on the phone, confident with patient communication, and experienced in US healthcare administrative workflows. The strongest candidate will be someone who can step into the role quickly, manage calls professionally, support Spanish-speaking patients, and help keep the clinic's front desk operations running smoothly.

title: Maintenance Controller
description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service - spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack - from the lab to the field - we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Air Mobility Group (AIRMOB) is responsible for developing and delivering Metrea’s aerial refueling (AAR) capabilities, ensuring the readiness and operational effectiveness of the tanker fleet. AIRMOB oversees fleet management, maintenance, and airworthiness, working to sustain and enhance refueling operations. It manages the integration of new processes and technologies, ensuring that tanker aircraft remain mission-ready through effective logistics, maintenance oversight, and regulatory compliance. By coordinating across various teams, AIRMOB ensures the fleet meets both current and future operational needs, supporting a range of specialized air mobility missions. 

Position Summary

The Maintenance Controller is responsible for coordinating and planning maintenance activities on their assigned shift for MSM's KC-135 fleet. This role ensures efficient execution of maintenance operations, provides technical support to maintenance activities, and maintains effective communication between Maintenance, Operations, and Logistics Departments. The position requires technical expertise in aviation maintenance and the ability to ensure compliance with FAA regulations and company policies while reporting directly to the Maintenance Control Manager. 

What You'll Do

• Coordinate and plan maintenance activities and provide technical support on assigned shift 

• Coordinate maintenance activities conducted by Contract Agencies, where applicable

• Ensure contracted maintenance personnel are properly briefed and understand the nature of problems to be worked, as well as company policies and procedures for maintenance activities

• Ensure all work is performed in accordance with current FARs, company manuals, and other Technical Data acceptable to the Administrator

• Provide technical assistance to all maintenance activities and personnel

• Monitor all DMIs (Deferred Maintenance Items) to ensure time limits are not exceeded

• Monitor, update, and verify aircraft status; report aircraft status changes as they occur to Operations and Maintenance

• Execute planning and scheduling of airframe and line engine maintenance/inspections, airworthiness directives, service bulletins, corrosion program requirements, scheduled modifications, and mandatory replacement items as directed

• Assemble Aircraft Maintenance/Insp

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!
Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.
This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.
Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly's operational and analytical systems.
This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.
What you will do

Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.

Natera is seeking an experienced Clinical Oncology Specialist (COS) to join our specialized Genitourinary (GU) Oncology sales team. This high-impact, tumor-specific role will focus on driving adoption and growth of  Signatera™, Natera's personalized, tumor-informed molecular residual disease (MRD) test , across the GU Oncology landscape.

Signatera is a circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay designed to detect molecular residual disease and monitor disease recurrence. title: Senior Blockchain Engineer (TEE)
description:
【岗位职责】

• 参与可信执行环境（TEE）相关模块的研发，包括可信执行、远程证明、密钥保护、安全隔离及可信计算任务执行。

• 参与数字资产托管系统、钱包系统、签名服务、密钥管理系统（KMS）或硬件安全模块（HSM）或链上资产安全相关产品的技术方案设计。

• 与后端研发、区块链及产品团队协同，按技术规范完成核心安全基础设施的开发与交付任务。

【任职要求】

• 计算机科学、信息安全、密码学、软件工程或相关专业本科及以上学历。

• 熟练掌握至少一种系统级开发语言（如 Rust / Go / C++ / C），具备良好的工程编码能力与系统落地能力。

• 熟悉 TEE 技术原理，并在至少一种实际开发环境中具备实践经验（如 Intel SGX、Open Enclave 或主流云厂商的机密计算环境）。

• 熟悉 Linux 环境开发，理解网络通信、并发编程、内存管理及系统调优等底层技术。

• 理解常见密码学原理，包括椭圆曲线密码学、哈希算法、数字签名、密钥协商、承诺方案、零知识证明基础等。

• 熟悉常见区块链的签名算法、地址体系或交易签名流程者优先。

• 具备良好的系统安全工程意识，能够准确分析攻击面、界定协议边界，并理解密钥生命周期管理与异常场景处理。

【工作地点与安排】

• 工作地点：新加坡。

• 办公模式：支持在新加坡本地进行远程办公。

• 签证支持：公司可为符合条件的海外候选人提供新加坡工作签证（EP）申请支持。

• 语言要求：团队工作语言主要为中文，需具备良好的英文技术文档阅读与撰写能力。

【申请方式】
请将完整的个人 PDF 版本简历发送至：jenna.wang@davionlabs.com
简历标题格式：姓名 - 【应聘Senior Blockchain Engineer】- 目前所在国家/城市
【公司概述】
Davion Labs 现诚邀一位熟悉可信执行环境（TEE）与密码学，且具备扎实底层系统开发经验的高级区块链工程师（TEE方向）加入 ApeX Protocol核心团队。
ApeX Protocol 是业内领先的去中心化交易所 (DEX) 平台，致力于为用户提供流畅、高效、安全的加密货币交易体验。我们专注于技术创新与用户赋能，旨在通过高可用架构与全面的产品组合，重新定义去中心化交易格局。
我们的核心产品 ApeX Omni (v2) 提供多链流动性、灵活且以用户为中心的设计，以及基于零知识证明等前沿技术的顶级安全保障。为了在高度去中心化的高频交易环境中彻底保障用户资产与数据的绝对安全，我们正在积极探索并构建基于机密计算技术的下一代密钥托管与安全基础设施。
作为核心区块链工程师，您将深度参与 ApeX 协议底层安全系统与数字资产保护架构的全流程建设。从 TEE 核心模块的研发落地、复杂的密钥生命周期管理，到核心签名服务与数字资产托管方案的技术攻坚，您都将发挥关键作用。我们期待您凭借深厚的底层工程底蕴、严谨的系统安全边界意识，以及对机密计算的深刻理解，与团队紧密协同，共同打造Web3 顶级安全基建。

title: Sr. People Operations Generalist
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Sr. People Generalist builds the operational backbone of the People team: the processes, systems, data, and policies that let us scale without adding complexity. This is a builder role, not an administrator role. You will turn work that runs on tribal knowledge and one-off fixes into documented, measured, repeatable programs with clear owners and controls.

You will be helping define the center of excellence model on the People team: the escalation point for employee matters, a data connoisseur that owns data fidelity , and the person who decides where work should live as the team matures from reactive support to a proactive shared-services model. You will lead cross-functional projects and use AI to shape the employee experience.

 

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

- Define the People Ops operating model: what is standardized and centralized, what stays with People Partners or other COEs, and how work transitions with continuity and measurement built in

- Assess the maturity of each core People process (onboarding, offboarding, job changes, comp cycles, leaves, time off, rotations) and run a roadmap to move each from ad hoc to documented, measured, and automated

- Be the operational partner to People Business Partners: execute reorgs, promotions, performance actions, and exits they drive; supply the data and process support behind their work

- Set standards for process design, documentation, SLAs, and handoffs; own the SOP library and knowledge base so answers live in a system

- Support the build of audit-ready controls (recurring data audits, approval trails, segregation of duties) for SOX

- Define service-quality metrics (ticket volume, resolution time, error rate, employee satisfaction) and use them to decide what to fix next

- Run proactive audits across Workday and connected systems to catch errors before they reach payroll, equity, or board reporting

- Serve as a functional Workday owner: business process design from requirements through configuration, testing, and post-launch iteration

- Use AI and low-code tools to prototype and ship People Ops automations; know when a gap needs a lightweight internal tool versus a technical build with IT or Systems

- Resolve the hardest cases in benefits, leaves, time off, rotations, and sensitive org changes with precision, empathy, and clear written communication

- Partner with Finance, Legal, IT, Recruiting, and Payroll on projects that mature processes and policies for the business

- Lead change management for process redesigns and new tools: communication, training, adoption tracking, and feedback

title: Staff Security Analyst (Governance and Trust)
description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role in a nutshell:

Chainguard is building the secure foundation for software development and deployment. Our Governance & Trust team makes sure the security practices behind that mission are effective, measurable, and worthy of our customers' trust.

We're hiring a senior practitioner to lead the compliance and trust side of that team. You'll run the execution of our external examinations (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, and a growing set of sector and regional certifications), own how we respond to customer security diligence, and run third-party risk operations. You'll lead the compliance and trust side of the team, which includes a public-sector compliance analyst and two customer-facing security analysts, with formal management of that group expected as the team grows.

This is not a checklist compliance role. Our operating model treats policies and controls as code, draws evidence from systems of record rather than screenshots, and uses AI agents for first-pass questionnaire responses and vendor triage. You'll be the person who decides what those systems need to produce, judges whether what they produce is right, and stands behind it with an auditor or a customer.

What you’ll do:

• Run the execution of Chainguard's external examinations end to end: the evidence calendar, population and completeness-and-accuracy requests, sample fulfilment, auditor status calls, and readiness assessment ahead of each cycle. Work with the Head of Governance & Trust on scope, control applicability, and auditor negotiation.

• Build and keep the working relationships with People, IT, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and Sales that evidence, populations, and remediation depend on. Compliance and trust at Chainguard runs across most of the company, and the function should not be chasing other teams for what it needs.

• Own customer security diligence: security questionnaires, customer audits, Trust Center content, and the multi-round assessments that regulated customers run. Set turnaround expectations with Sales that the team can meet, and decide what we will and won't provide.

• Own the third-party risk management program: vendor intake and tiering, assessments, dispositions, and the register of critical suppliers and their agreements.

• Act as product owner for the customer-facing side of our agent platform: define what the questionnaire responder and vendor triage agents must do, maintain the validated answer bank they draw on, and judge whether their output is good enough to send. Stay current on how other companies handle diligence and response automation, and bring in better approaches when they exist.

• Turn recurring patterns across questionnaires, audits, and vendor reviews into standing artifacts, self-serve packages, and control improvements, so the same question is answered once.

• Work from a single unified controls catalog across frameworks, and push mapping and implementation defects back to the governance side rather than maintaining framework-specific lists.

• Produce findings and remediation evidence that survive external re-test, and feed the corrective-action process with root causes rather than symptoms.

• Guide the public-sector compliance analyst's work on assessor relationships and customer-facing federal diligence, with technical scoping decisions staying with the Head of Gove

title: Instrumentation Development Embedded Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

- You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

- You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

- Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

- Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

As the Instrumentation Development Embedded Engineer, you will own the development of high-speed control and protection systems for the Alpha fusion demonstrator, focusing on FPGA-based solutions for plasma heating hardware protection.

You will work across the full development lifecycle, from writing and verifying HDL code to developing software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing, integrating embedded software and electronics, and establishing robust development and deployment pipelines.

You will also help establish Proxima’s FPGA development capability beyond plasma heating, defining reusable architectures, development workflows, testing methodologies, and HDL best practices that can be adopted across other systems.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Design, implement, and maintain HDL-based control and protection systems, starting with plasma heating system protection.

- Establish end-to-end FPGA development workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and SIL/HIL test environments integrated with plant design frameworks.

- Develop embedded software, firmware, and low-level drivers to interface FPGAs with sensors, actuators, and other control systems.

- Collaborate across RF, controls, electronics, and systems teams to define system interfaces, ICDs, and verification plans.

WHO YOU ARE

- Degree in Electronics, Embedded Systems, or equivalent practical experience.

- Strong proficiency in HDL (VHDL, Verilog, SystemVerilog) and software scripting (Python, C/C++).

- Proven experience integrating FPGAs with hardware peripherals, board-level electronics, and communication interfaces.

- Familiarity with modern software development practices (Git, CI, code review, automated testing).

- Systems-thinking approach with strong debugging skills spanning HDL, embedded firmware, and physical hardware.

Nice to have:

- High-speed digital interfaces (multi-gigabit serial links, LVDS, SerDes, RF/instrumentation links) and PCB-level signal integrity.

- FPGA+processor platforms and MPSoCs (e.g., AMD/Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+).

- Precision timing and synchronization (IEEE 1588 PTP, White Rabbit)

- Network protocols (Ethernet).

- Real-time signal processing, fast protection systems, and high-speed data acquisition in fusion or industrial environments.

- HDL design methodologies and techniques for reliable radiation-hardened systems.

- Schematic comprehension and custom PCB development.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

- Technical Screening (30 min)

- Technical Panel (3x60 min)

title: Co-Op, Bayesian Methods for Complex Decision Making
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences builds AI systems that accelerate discovery across the physical and life sciences. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next.

Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search.

As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns.

What You'll Be Building

• Design and benchmark experiment-selection strategies that balance exploration and exploitation under realistic budgets

• Build autonomous discovery agents that propose the next experiment from surrogate models

• Develop in-context learning approaches inspired by Bayesian inference, evaluating calibration and robustness

• Run retrospective and live evaluations on active campaign data with clear baselines and metrics

• Present findings to ML and experimental teams, with the option to contribute to a publication

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Pursuing a Master's or PhD in statistics, ML, CS, operations research, applied math, or a quantitative science

• Solid grounding in Bayesian inference and decision making, including priors and posterior predictive distributions

• Research experience in Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, bandits, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modeling

• Strong Python skills with PyTorch and probabilistic libraries such as Pyro, PyMC, or BoTorch

• Comfort working with small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets

• Clear communication with both ML and experimental collaborators

Bonus Points For

• Applying these methods to real problems in materials science, chemistry, or another physical science

• Familiarity with in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference, meta-learning, or prior-data fitted networks

• Optimization over categorical or combinatorial spaces, including mixed-variable, multi-objective, or batch settings

• Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making or Bayesian experimental design

• Training models on multimodal scientific data such as text, images, spectra, or simulations

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

We’re All In

title: Infrastructure Solutions Architect - OEM
description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology-and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIA N, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.
We are looking for an Infrastructure Solutions Architect to help revolutionize computing. At NVIDIA , we encourage an inclusive and collaborative environment where ambitious individuals can grow. Our dedication to innovation and excellence has made us a leader in technology. We are now seeking outstanding talent to join us on this journey.
What you’ll be doing:

• Serve as the senior technical point of contact for OEM Federal deployments of NVIDIA GPU-accelerated platforms, including PCIe GPUs, HGX, and MGX systems, addressing any blocking issues.

• Own Issues End to End: Take responsibility for customer issues from start to finish - prioritizing platform, firmware, and workload problems. Drive these issues through the OEM's support tiers into NVIDIA engineering with the necessary logs and reproduction details to identify the root cause. Follow through with the customer until resolution.

• Failure Analysis & RMA: Establish and complete diagnostic, RMA eligibility, and replacement procedures for Federal deployments. This includes situations where failed hardware and logs must remain on-site at the customer facility.

• Navigate Federal security frameworks including FedRAMP, IL5/IL6, and air-gapped (SCIF) environments, and help the customer meet sanitization and chain-of-custody requirements for hardware returns.

• Partner with OEM Federal support and services teams to reduce blocking issues and unnecessary dispatches. Detail failure signatures to build the Federal knowledge base and apply AI tools where the environment allows.

What we need to see:

• Due to the classified nature of the work, the selected candidate must be a U.S. citizen and possess and maintain an active U.S. Government TS/SCI clearance. Certain Intelligence Community customer assignments may also require a current U.S. Government-administered Counterintelligence Scope or Full Scope Polygraph.

• BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience

• 5+ years of engineering experience on multi-GPU platforms, including at least 3 years in a customer-facing support, field engineering, or blocking issue role.

• Strong system software expertise across firmware, BIOS, kernel, drivers, and operating systems, with the ability to troubleshoot, optimize, and customize Linux environments for AI/ML workloads.

• Expert knowledge of data center infrastructure - x86/ARM systems, high-performance storage, and low-latency networking (InfiniBand/RDMA).

• Professional-level communication and organizational skills, including adjusting to the technical level of the audience, staying calm and focused in negative situations, and driving issues through to closure.

• This role requires up to 35% travel to customer, partner, and data center sites, including secure facilities, and occasional weekend and holiday coverage.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Dell Ecosystem Expertise: Proven experience with Dell PowerEdge GPU servers and Dell's management software (OpenManage, APEX), and familiarity with Dell's support and process for handling blocking issues.

• Federal Mission Experience: Direct experience supporting DoD, Intelligence Community, or Civilian agency deployments, and comfort operating within their security and logistics constraints.

title: VP, Data Engineering

description:
The brands on your kitchen shelf are run by people doing extraordinary work that nobody sees.

We're building the platform they run on, and a brand they'll be proud to be part of.

Confido is the AI operating system that runs cash application, deductions, trade and planning in one place for CPG brands. That means Finance, Sales, and Ops finally work on the same number.

We’re trusted by 250+ brands managing $30B+ in revenue, including Daisy, OLIPOP, Simple Mills, Idahoan, and more. We've achieved best-in-class growth and recently raised a $55M Series B led by Insight Partners to accelerate our momentum.

If you want your work on shelves everywhere - and outsized ownership while you build - we'd love to meet you.

THE ROLE

Data at Confido feeds customer-facing reports, internal dashboards, and a lot of day-to-day decisions. Right now it lives in too many places and is owned by too many people. We’re hiring a VP of Data Engineering to own all of it: how data gets into our systems, how it’s stored and modeled, and how it shows up in the reports people use, inside the company and out.

You’ll be the single owner of data at Confido. You’ll manage our Senior Analytics Engineer to start, and you’ll build the team from there. Early on you’ll be hands-on. Over time, more of your time will go to hiring, setting direction, and working with the leadership team.

What You’ll Own

- Ingestion. Every source that feeds our data, including product databases, event tracking, and third-party tools. You decide how data comes in, how often, and what happens when a source changes or breaks.

- Warehouse and pipelines. Warehouse design, orchestration, and the infrastructure underneath, including its cost.

- Modeling. One set of core models and metric definitions that the whole company uses.

- Reporting. Internal dashboards and BI, plus the data behind customer-facing reports. If a number shows up somewhere at Confido, it’s yours.

- Quality and governance. Testing, monitoring, access controls, and data privacy. You’re accountable when numbers are wrong, and you put fixes in place so the same problems don’t come back.

What You’ll Do

- Build and lead the data org, starting with our Senior Analytics Engineer. Decide which roles to hire and when, run the interviews, and develop the people you bring on.

- Set the data roadmap and explain the trade-offs to the leadership team and the rest of the company.

- Make the big technical calls on architecture, tooling, and build vs. buy.

- Work with Engineering, Product, Ops, and Customer teams to figure out what data they actually need, and say no when something isn’t worth building.

- Set the standards the team works by: modeling, testing, docs, monitoring, and on-call.

- Write SQL, review PRs, and build things yourself while the team is small.

What We’re Looking For

- 10+ years in data engineering, analytics engineering, or similar, with 4+ years leading data teams.

- You’ve owned data end to end before, from ingestion through reporting, not just one layer of it.

- You’ve built a data function from an early or messy state, grown the team, and kept it running.

- Strong SQL and data modeling skills, and experience with Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Dagster, or similar tools.

- You’ve hired well, including people senior to where the team started.

- You can sit in a leadership meeting, turn “we need better data” into a plan, and defend it.

- You’re comfortable being hands-on now and stepping back as the team grows.

Success in This Role

A year in, there’s no question about who owns data at Confido. People trust the numbers and know where to find them. Sources are documented, pipelines break less often, and when they do, the team catches it before a customer does. Internal and customer-facing reports run off the same definitions. The team has grown, it has a clear structure and standards, and it’s planned out for the next stage.

• Lead value creation workshops and define measures to improve process inefficiencies

• Define and build KPIs measuring the customer’s success and quantify business impact

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.
Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

• Own Group positioning, corporate narratives and communications around major company developments.

• Work with business leaders to translate strategy into specific priorities, investments and execution plans.

What you will need

• Strong strategy experience in a technology company, high-growth startup, strategy, consulting investment environment or your own startup.

• Experience developing and executing strategies with measurable business outcomes.

• Strong commercial and financial judgement with the ability to evaluate markets, businesses and investments.

• Strong analytical capability and ability to build business cases and financial models directly.

• Excellent written communication and ability to turn complex business topics into clear narratives.

• Experience with corporate development, investments, M&A or corporate communications is useful.

• Hands-on operating style - able to research, analyse, write and drive strategic work personally.
